itinerary.summary: Churches, Latin-quarter lanes and a riverside sunset.

place.name: Basilica of Bom Jesus and Old Goa
place.description: UNESCO-listed churches from Goa's Portuguese capital, including the Basilica holding St Francis Xavier's relics and the vast Sé Cathedral.

place.name: Fontainhas Latin Quarter
place.description: Walk the yellow, blue and red houses of Panjim's old Portuguese quarter, then a fish-thali lunch at a local canteen.

afternoon.tip: Ritz Classic and Anandashram are local favourites for fish thali.

place.name: Miramar Beach sunset
place.description: The city's beach where the Mandovi meets the sea; locals come for evening walks and corn-on-the-cob carts.

evening.tip: Rent a scooter for the trip today (₹300-400 a day) and keep your licence handy.

itinerary.summary: Cabo de Rama, Palolem and a boat to Butterfly Beach.

place.name: Cabo de Rama Fort
place.description: A crumbling clifftop fort with a little church and huge views over the Arabian Sea, rarely busy.

morning.tip: The road is quiet but winding; ride carefully.

place.name: Palolem Beach
place.description: A crescent of sand lined with palms and huts, calm enough for swimming in winter.

afternoon.tip: Lunch at a beach shack; prices drop the further you walk from the main entrance.

place.name: Boat to Butterfly Beach
place.description: Share a fishing boat to a hidden cove reachable only by sea, with dolphin sightings often on the way.

evening.tip: Shared boats are cheapest; negotiate at the north end of Palolem.

itinerary.summary: Fort Aguada, the Anjuna flea market and Vagator's cliffs.

place.name: Fort Aguada
place.description: A 17th-century Portuguese fort and lighthouse guarding the Mandovi estuary.

morning.tip: Go early before the heat and the tour buses.

place.name: Anjuna Flea Market
place.description: The Wednesday market by the beach: textiles, silver, spices and a mix of traders from across India.

afternoon.tip: It runs on Wednesdays in season (Nov-Apr); on other days, Mapusa's Friday market is the local alternative.

place.name: Chapora Fort and Vagator
place.description: Climb to the 'Dil Chahta Hai' fort for sunset over Vagator's red cliffs and the Chapora river.

evening.tip: Wear grippy shoes; the laterite path is loose.

stays.name: Zostel Goa (Anjuna)
stays.why: Social hostel near the flea market, with dorms and private rooms.

stays.name: Palolem beach huts
stays.why: Simple huts steps from the sand, the classic budget south-Goa stay.

stays.name: Panjim Inn
stays.why: A 19th-century mansion in the Latin quarter, good value for a splurge night.

essentials.currency: Indian Rupee (INR). UPI and cards work in towns; carry cash for small temples, coracles and rural stalls.
essentials.language: Konkani; English and Hindi widely spoken
essentials.tipping: Round up at shacks; 5-10% in restaurants
essentials.weather: Nov-Feb is peak and dry (21-32°C). Jun-Sep is monsoon; many shacks close.
essentials.gettingAround: Rent a scooter (₹300-400/day) and wear a helmet; GoaMiles app taxis for longer hops.

packing: Light rain jacket if travelling at season edges

summary.overview: Goa on a backpacker budget: scooter-hopping between the quieter south beaches, Portuguese lanes in Panjim's Fontainhas, a flea market, and fish thalis that cost less than a coffee back home.
highlights: Scootering to Palolem and Butterfly Beach
